briefings.title: Algorithmic Storytelling
briefings.tldr: Multidisciplinary artist Victoria Fard uses custom 3D algorithms to craft monumental "digital sanctuaries" that merge technology with human memory, inviting public audiences to pause and experience shared moments of awe.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Multidisciplinary artist Victoria Fard uses custom 3D algorithms to craft monumental "digital sanctuaries" that merge technology with human memory, inviting public audiences to pause and experience shared moments of awe. Rather than relying on automated generative AI, Fard advocates for human-controlled technology that prioritizes emotional resonance, physical scale, and universal public accessibility.

## The Philosophy of Digital Sanctuaries and Public Art

* **Defining Digital Sanctuaries:** Fard designs immersive, digital environments inspired by nature, culture, and architecture to offer viewers places to pause, be present, and experience reality differently.
* **Transitioning Observers to Participants:** The goal of spatial, digital storytelling is to shift the viewer from a passive observer to an active participant whose attention is completely absorbed by the atmosphere.
* **Democratizing Art via Public Spaces:** Fard advocates that art should meet people in their daily lives rather than existing only in ticketed or planned-visit venues.
    * **Times Square Installation (July 2023):** Displayed on over 100 screens for three minutes nightly, Fard’s work brought a rare collective stillness to over 2 million in-person and online viewers in one of the world's most sensory-heavy locations.
    * **The Outernet (London):** Fard exhibited her work on free, publicly accessible, four-story-high screens operating on a massive 16,000-resolution canvas to allow pedestrians to walk in and experience art unexpectedly.

## The Creative Process: Human Intention vs. Algorithmic Automation

* **The Value of Sweat Equity:** Each digital world takes between six months to a year to complete, yielding project files that can exceed 700 gigabytes of data. 
* **Custom Algorithms vs. Generative AI:** Fard deliberately chooses not to use generative AI in her creative work, identifying a key limitation in its predictability and micro-level control.
    * **The Controllability Issue:** By writing her own scripts and parameters, Fard maintains absolute control over the geometry generated by the system.
    * **The Human Element:** Fard emphasizes that systems cannot understand *why* a choice matters because they lack lived experiences, cultural backgrounds, and memories.
    * **Human-Driven Decisions:** While technology acts as her "paintbrush," the artist makes thousands of active decisions on what to keep, remove, and allow to exist.

## Scaling, Interactivity, and Future Collaborations

* **The Impact of Physical Scale:** Massive displays are critical to Fard's work because they physically engage the viewer. A piece viewed on an iPhone lacks the bodily impact of a 16K, four-story installation.
* **Integrating Augmented Reality (AR):** To push past purely visual experiences, Fard collaborated with the tech company Augmento and the World Economic Forum to integrate her piece, *Momentum*, into an AR environment where users can physically walk through and explore the digital space.
* **Combining Storytelling with Music:** During the session, Zhang Jinjun, a museum curator, proposed a future integration of Fard's digital environments with orchestral and historical music (such as Beethoven or ancient Chinese chimes) to deepen the cross-cultural and sensory impact of her sanctuaries.

## Sustaining Creative Imagination and Preventing Burnout

* **Cultivating Daily Imagination:** Fard draws her creative resilience from family values, the experience of being a new mother, and remaining open to learning from different languages, cultures, and travels.
* **Strategies for Managing Burnout:** For creative professionals navigating high-pressure projects, Fard highlights key practices for longevity:
    * **Listen to the Body:** Recognize when it is time to rest rather than trying to force productivity.
    * **Practice Self-Grace:** Understand that artists cannot control every variable, and giving oneself the grace to recover actually builds the strength to complete projects excellently.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "Storytelling isn't only about what is created, it is about how it is experienced." — Victoria Fard

> "The system does not recognize why one choice matters more than the other. It has never walked into a cathedral, it has never traveled, nor has it ever carried a memory of a place. That belongs to me." — Victoria Fard

> "I don't think that storytelling is being reinvented. I think it is expanding. Technology allows stories to be shared more immersively... But the tools will change, especially with AI. The meaning comes from our human experience, our intention, our values, our memories, and the things we pay attention to." — Victoria Fard

briefings.title: Ali Ghodsi, Co-founder and CEO, Databricks kicks off Data + AI Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: At the Data + AI Summit 2026, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi declared that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) has arrived, shifting the enterprise challenge from "intelligence" to "context."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
At the Data + AI Summit 2026, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi declared that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) has arrived, shifting the enterprise challenge from "intelligence" to "context." To resolve this, Databricks introduced a suite of open, agentic platform innovations designed to transform the lakehouse into the future "agentic system of record" while solving critical hurdles in choice, cost, and control.

***

## The Shift to the "Agentic System of Record"
*   **The Context Problem:** While frontier AI models can solve hyper-complex academic problems, they struggle inside enterprises because they lack real-time corporate context. 
    *   **The Live-Loop Bottleneck:** Current agents perform slow, expensive, and low-accuracy "random walks" across document folders and disconnected APIs.
    *   **Four Pillars of Resolution:** To scale AI, enterprises must solve for **Choice** (avoiding model/cloud lock-in), **Control** (governance and security), **Cost** (preventing runaway token budgets), and **Context** (indexing corporate knowledge).
*   **Evolution of the SaaS Stack:** Traditional SaaS stacks isolate data in proprietary systems of record. Databricks argues the future belongs to a unified **Agentic System of Record** where all data, security, and AI models reside on a single, open data platform across multiple clouds.

## Unleashing Enterprise Context: Genie Ontology & Agent Suite
*   **Genie Ontology:** A major architectural breakthrough that automatically constructs a background knowledge graph of an organization’s entire data estate.
    *   **OntoRank Algorithm:** Developed by Databricks’ research team, this algorithm acts like "PageRank for enterprise assets." It maps connections across structured databases, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, and org charts.
    *   **Unity Catalog Semantics:** Integrates manual business glossaries and curated semantic layers from partners like Atlan and AtScale.
*   **The Genie Agent Portfolio:**
    *   **Genie One:** A unified, secure, consumer-grade search and chat interface for all business users to access company-wide data via mobile or desktop.
    *   **Genie Agents:** Converts standard user-Genie conversations into deployable, automated agents that integrate into Slack or Microsoft Teams (e.g., automated HR assistants).
    *   **Genie Code:** An agent specialized in low-level data engineering, pipeline writing, and training machine learning models on GPUs.
    *   **Genie ZeroOps:** A background operations agent that automatically detects broken data pipelines at night, tests code corrections in a sandbox, and sends a "one-click fix" push notification to on-call engineers.
*   **Agent Bricks & Omnigent:** A developer sandbox environment featuring "Agent Memory" and **Omnigent**—an open-source meta-harness developed by Matei Zaharia that pits different frontier models against each other to optimize output quality.

## Open Data Architecture, Lakebase, and Unified Governance
*   **Data Format Convergence:** Databricks announced the GA of Apache Iceberg V3 support within Databricks Runtime (DBR), achieving a unified data layer that prevents the need to rewrite files between Iceberg and Delta Lake. Delta 5 and Iceberg V4 (targeted for Q4 2026) will finalize the unified metadata layer.
*   **Lakebase Postgres:** An open-source transaction processing engine (OLTP) that separates compute from storage, utilizing cheap lake storage.
    *   **Serverless Autoscaling:** Scales Postgres down to zero when inactive, significantly reducing Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).
    *   **Database Branching:** Allows agents or developers to clone petabyte-scale databases in less than a second using copy-on-write, enabling zero-risk sandbox experimentation.
*   **Unity AI Gateway:** A new, open-source control pane within Unity Catalog and MLflow to curb runaway AI costs and manage agent access.
    *   **Token Spend Management:** Provides unified capacity purchasing, allowing companies to spend their Databricks contract dollars directly on frontier models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) while enforcing strict departmental budgets and rate limits.
*   **OpenSharing:** An open-source project superseding Delta Sharing. It allows companies to securely share Delta/Iceberg tables, AI models, skills, and autonomous agents across organizations and on-premises environments.

## Next-Generation Agentic Applications & Acquisitions
*   **Acquisition of Panther Labs:** Databricks has agreed to acquire Panther Labs, a Python-based SIEM platform. Founded by Jack Naglieri, Panther's Pythonic detection framework aligns natively with LLMs, which naturally generate and read Python code.
*   **Lakewatch:** An agentic, cost-effective Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system built directly on the security lakehouse. It uses autonomous agents to triage high-volume alerts and hunt for zero-day exploits.
*   **CustomerLake:** An agentic Customer Data Platform (CDP) featuring an LLM-driven Profile Agent for identity de-duplication, and a Campaign Agent designed to run hyper-personalized "Infinity Campaigns."
*   **Lakeflow Upgrades:** Introduzes **ZeroBus** (GA) for high-rate, brokerless streaming ingestion; **Spark Real-Time Mode (RTM)** for sub-second streaming latencies; and **Lakeflow Designer** (GA) for visual data engineering.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "AGI is already here. It’s plenty smart. We don't need it to be more intelligent... The problem we have is that AGI is not really completely permeating our organizations."
> — Ali Ghodsi

> "You shouldn't have to care about formats. You should be able to use whatever tools you want with all of your data... We are very close to the full unification vision."
> — Ryan Blue

> "In the next 12 months, we're going to see more software be written than ever in the history of mankind... All that software that your organizations are going to write using LLMs and coding tools need a database behind the scenes."
> — Ali Ghodsi

briefings.title: Building Startup Cities - Balaji Srinivasan | #84
briefings.tldr: Faced with declining societal trust, failing centralized governance, and a looming $193.6 trillion US fiscal crisis, builders are moving away from traditional mega-cities to pioneer opt-in "startup cities" and "network states."
briefings.summary_markdown:
1. **TL;DR**  
Faced with declining societal trust, failing centralized governance, and a looming $193.6 trillion US fiscal crisis, builders are moving away from traditional mega-cities to pioneer opt-in "startup cities" and "network states." By leveraging cryptographic social contracts, decentralized real estate investment trusts (REITs), and off-grid modular technologies, these new communities are restoring self-governance and economic alignment through peaceful competition.

***

## The Rise of Startup Cities and Opt-In Societies

* **The Flight from One-Party States:** **Balaji Srinivasan** argues that major blue states like California have devolved into non-consensual, one-party systems that fail to deliver results. 
    * **Exit as Voice:** To restore true democracy, citizens are "voting with their feet" by moving to alternative startup societies rather than trying to fix broken centralized political systems.
* **The Ridgerunner Creed:** **Josh Abbotoy** describes his Tennessee-based project, Ridgerunner LLC, as a neighborhood-level effort centered on traditional Appalachian living and a simple ethos: "faith, family, freedom."
    * **Fostering Autonomy:** Ridgerunner aims to create spaces (churches, schools, community centers) where families can escape hyper-consumerism and build self-determining, high-trust environments.
* **Techno-Democracy and On-Chain Consent:** Srinivasan proposes formalizing physical community entry through digital, "social smart contracts" at the border.
    * **Contractual Governance:** By signing a public, cryptographic terms-of-service agreement to enter a community, residents make an active, visible commitment to uphold communal rules, combining left-libertarian consent with right-libertarian contract.
* **The Network School Model:** Located on a man-made island near Singapore, Srinivasan's Network School serves as a physical-meets-digital hub where 300 founders and builders from over 100 countries co-live and co-work for $1,500 a month. 
    * **Open-Source Playbook:** The school is a practical test case for the "Network State" theory, aiming to open-source its templates so other communities globally can replicate its success.

## Quantifying Trust and "Skin in the Game"

* **The Collapse of Social Trust:** **Nate Fischer** emphasizes that high-trust environments are rare and highly valuable commodities in an era of failing centralized institutions. 
    * **The Root of Decay:** Mass democracy fails because a growing share of the population lacks "skin in the game," voting instead for short-term handouts that deplete social capital.
* **Time as Skin in the Game:** Fischer highlights physical proximity and shared time as foundational social technologies. Regularly showing up to local institutions (like churches or community groups) builds a reputational credit reservoir that online-only spaces struggle to replicate.
* **The "Man-Month" Metric:** To measure community depth, Srinivasan introduces the concept of multiplying the number of people by the duration of their stay. 
    * **Proven Scale:** The Network School has generated nearly 500 "man-years" of co-living over 18 months, proving that virtual networks can successfully transition into dense, high-trust physical interactions.
* **Rebuilding the Web of Trust:** Modern communities can utilize Web3 cryptographic technology to map decentralized identity. Unlike AI-generative systems, cryptography cannot be faked, allowing physical communities to safely vet and onboard members using verified on-chain references.

## Solving the "Upside vs. Utility" Dilemma in Real Estate

* **The Network Orchestration Challenge:** Startup cities face a classic cold-start problem: a new town with 100 people lacks the utility (stores, restaurants, schools) of a mega-city like Singapore or New York.
* **The Crypto REIT Solution:** To incentivize early adopters to take the risk of moving to a low-utility community, Srinivasan suggests issuing "crypto equity" or shares in a community-wide REIT.
    * **Aligning Incentives:** Just as early equity offset WhatsApp's initial lack of utility and token airdrops grew Bitcoin's global network, giving early pioneers a financial stake in the *entire* community's growth mitigates NIMBYism and spurs rapid collective development.
* **Land Ownership vs. Shared Equity:** Abbotoy and Fischer note that while tokenized REITs solve rent-seeking, traditional land ownership remains highly attractive. Owning 20 to 30 acres in Appalachia gives families a profound sense of sovereignty and agency, acting as a physical hedge against urban instability.
* **The Solar and Modular Singularity:** Rapid advancements in modular construction and cheap, shatterproof solar energy are paving the way for off-grid, cost-effective villages.
    * **Modular Levittowns:** Communities can deploy cheap, high-quality residential, gym, and church units quickly, reducing the cost of housing to the price of a car while reducing vulnerability to state infrastructure failures.

## Macro Geopolitics: America's $193.6 Trillion Debt and Global Realignment

* **The True US Fiscal Crisis:** Srinivasan highlights a devastating metric from the US Government's Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Report: **$193.6 trillion in unfunded Medicare and Social Security liabilities** (calculated in present-value terms).
    * **Rapid Debt Accrual:** This represents a massive jump from $175.3 trillion in 2024, equating to roughly $600,000 in debt per citizen, or $6 million per top taxpayer.
* **De-Dollarization and Military Retreat:** Historically, US profligacy was offset by global dollar dominance and the military projection of 750 global bases. This system is breaking down due to the "precision strike revolution" (drones and cheap missiles making US carriers and bases sitting ducks).
    * **Shrinking Tax Base:** As the US military withdraws and allies seek alternative security arrangements, the true tax base for "dollar inflation" is shrinking rapidly, paving the way for domestic price spikes and energy crises.
* **The Return of Historical Parity:** For thousands of years, the Eurasian landmass held economic and military parity. The post-WWII unipolar American hegemony was a historical anomaly. With Russia, China, and India embracing market dynamics over socialism/communism, the global economy is reverting to its historical, multipolar baseline.

## Cultural Cohesion and the "Code and Cloud" Identity

* **The Shift from Market to Competitor:** Srinivasan observes that since 2024, Western tech elites have undergone a psychological shift. They no longer view rising global talent (particularly from India and China) as a vast market to capture, but as direct competition.
* **Code and Cloud vs. Blood and Soil:** In response to rising ethnic and nationalistic tensions within the US, Srinivasan defines his allegiance by class rather than race or geography. He identifies as a "code and cloud" person rather than a "blood and soil" nationalist.
    * **Peace and Trade:** Rather than engaging in political or cultural conflict, the goal of the network state movement is to foster peaceful, mutually beneficial trade between distinct, self-governing cultural nodes (e.g., "apple farmers trading with orange farmers").

***

## Notable Quotes

> "We are restoring democracy by having people have the consent of the governed... If you have cooperation and if you have consent and you have contract, you don't have coercion."  
> — **Balaji Srinivasan**

> "Mass democracy fails because many people... don't have any meaningful skin in the game in a sense. They're voting, they're often voting for something that is pure handouts... If you essentially have your society run by people who are just trying to take from other people, you're inevitably going to destroy the trust that exists in society."  
> — **Nate Fischer**

> "When you own 30 acres in Appalachia, you are functionally like a king on those 30 acres. You have a feeling of sovereignty. There's so much that you can do that nobody can stop you from doing and you have real agency and freedom."  
> — **Josh Abbotoy**

> "I don't want to fight other Americans... Just like the English who left for Massachusetts and left for Virginia, they didn't want to spend their lives dying in the English Civil War... Instead, the smart guys, the proto-Americans, exited and built their own thing."  
> — **Balaji Srinivasan**

briefings.title: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen’s $56B Plan to Take Over eBay
briefings.tldr: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen outlines a $56 billion strategic vision to acquire and revitalize eBay by applying his signature high-efficiency operating playbook, cutting $2 billion in redundant costs, and repairing alienated seller relationships to scale a dominant global marketplace for collectibles and second-hand goods.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen outlines a $56 billion strategic vision to acquire and revitalize eBay by applying his signature high-efficiency operating playbook, cutting $2 billion in redundant costs, and repairing alienated seller relationships to scale a dominant global marketplace for collectibles and second-hand goods.

## The Operational Playbook: From Chewy to GameStop

* **The Chewy Origin Story:** Ryan Cohen scaled Chewy into a highly sticky, recurring-revenue business model to compete directly with Amazon.
  * **Efficiency Focus:** The pet food category is a low-margin "game of pennies" that required aggressive vendor negotiations, zero-tolerance policies on overpaying suppliers, and optimized logistics to achieve a $3.35 billion exit.
  * **Hiring Philosophy:** Cohen prioritizes "will over skill," seeking highly motivated, relentless "diehards" over candidates who only look qualified on paper.
* **The GameStop Turnaround:** After taking a active board role and eventually stepping in as CEO in 2023, Cohen corrected early strategic mistakes of trying to make GameStop an e-commerce-first business like Amazon.
  * **Pivoting to Physical Strengths:** He transitioned GameStop’s focus toward cost-cutting, retail execution, and high-margin physical collectibles and Trading Card Games (TCG).
  * **Financial Results:** GameStop's collectible division now makes up 42% of revenue ($350 million in Q1 out of $835 million total). The company holds $9.7 billion in cash, generated $333 million in free cash flow, and reduced SG&A from $228 million to $202 million.

## The Strategic Rationale for Acquiring eBay

* **Complementary Strengths:** GameStop and eBay share overlapping strengths in the secondary market, second-hand authentication, and collectibles. What GameStop executes in physical retail (such as giving immediate cash for graded PSA 8+ cards), eBay scales globally online.
* **Targeting Circle of Competence:** Cohen views eBay as a fundamentally strong business model that falls directly within his expertise in digital marketplace dynamics and e-commerce.
* **Low-Risk Marketplace Model:** Unlike Chewy or Amazon, Cohen has no desire to build out a massive first-party logistics and inventory network for eBay. He intends to keep eBay as an asset-light, third-party marketplace.

## Diagnosing eBay’s Institutional Decline

* **Stagnant Metrics and Bleeding Users:** Despite a strong first-mover advantage, eBay has failed to keep pace with e-commerce growth.
  * Since the pandemic, the platform has lost 30 million active users.
  * Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) and operating earnings are down, while operating expenses have bloated to over half of total revenues.
* **Alienation of Key Sellers:** Under professional, non-founder management, eBay has treated its power sellers—the true "customers" of a marketplace—with complacency.
  * Management eliminated dedicated seller concierge programs.
  * A lack of native tools forces sellers to rely on expensive third-party software integrations to run their businesses.
* **Consultant Culture:** Cohen criticizes eBay's current leadership for relying on high-priced external consulting firms rather than rolling up their sleeves to solve engineering and platform issues directly with sellers.

## Cohen's Three-Part Vision to Rebuild eBay

* **Part 1: Immediate Cost Extraction:** Cohen intends to immediately pull $2 billion in operating costs out of eBay to streamline the business and significantly boost earnings.
* **Part 2: Expanding Live Commerce:** Integrating robust live-shopping features to reclaim market share lost to younger, nimbler category-specific competitors.
* **Part 3: Digital and Physical Collectible Ecosystem:** Building a digital, in-game collectible trading marketplace that bridges the gap between digital gaming assets and physical collectibles.
* **Seller-First Engineering:** Establishing a direct pipeline between top sellers and eBay's engineering team to systematically eliminate seller pain points and build better native management tools.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "If our suppliers are sending us gifts in the mail, that's a really bad sign. It means we're overpaying. If our suppliers are telling us they never want to speak to us again, it means we're getting the right price." — Ryan Cohen

> "In a marketplace model like eBay, the sellers are the customer. You make your sellers happy, you give them the tools, they bring more inventory online, and you end up ultimately doing more sales... It's not that complicated." — Ryan Cohen

> "GameStop I don't think was such a good idea [in hindsight]... This [eBay] is actually a really good idea, whether it ends up working out or not. This is within my circle of competence, and I can't stop thinking about it." — Ryan Cohen

briefings.title: HBM 넘어 '3D 적층' HBS 시대 열린다?… "AI 꿈의 반도체, 주인공은 삼전-SK하닉 될 것"[머니가이드 for 영올드 Ep.33 김정호]
briefings.tldr: KAIST Professor Kim Jung-ho projects that the AI memory paradigm will evolve from current HBM through HBF and ultimately to the ultra-advanced HBS, establishing Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to dominate a potential 600 trillion KRW operating profit era driven by custom AI memory demand.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
- **TL;DR:** KAIST Professor Kim Jung-ho projects that the AI memory paradigm will evolve from current HBM through HBF and ultimately to the ultra-advanced HBS, establishing Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to dominate a potential 600 trillion KRW operating profit era driven by custom AI memory demand.

---

## Evolution of AI Memory: HBM, HBF, and HBS
- **HBM (High Bandwidth Memory):** Solves both capacity and speed bottlenecks in AI by vertically stacking DRAM and utilizing massive parallel structures (1,024 to 2,048+ data lanes).
  - *Dr. Kim Jung-ho* notes that while HBM began in the 2010s for graphics cards and TV displays, it became the cornerstone of AI due to deep learning and matrix math.
- **HBF (High Bandwidth Flash):** Stacks NAND Flash instead of DRAM to handle massive context expansion, KV-caching, and multi-agent AI workloads requiring 1,000x more memory.
  - *Dr. Kim Jung-ho* predicts HBF demand will eventually surpass HBM roughly 10 years out (around the time of HBM8 in 2038), coexisting in a multi-tiered memory complex alongside HBM.
- **HBS (High Bandwidth SRAM):** A newly proposed wafer-scale concept by *Dr. Kim Jung-ho* that vertically stacks SRAM layers to achieve 1,000x faster speeds with sufficient capacity for wafer-scale AI chips like Cerebras.

## The Shift from Training to Inference and Memory-Centric Computing
- **Inference Shift:** The AI paradigm has transitioned from training to inference, where memory capacity and retrieval speed matter far more than raw GPU compute power to prevent hallucinations and support personalized AI (AIPC, AI smartphones).
- **GPU Bottleneck:** *Dr. Kim Jung-ho* notes that GPUs operate at only 10% to 20% utilization because they spend most of their time waiting for data from traditional memory.
- **Memory-Centric Architecture:** To solve this, computing is moving inside the memory stack (Memory-Centric Computing), starting with HBM4 integrating GPU/CPU logic functions directly into the lower tiers of the memory stack.

## Market Dynamics, Competitors, and Geopolitical Risks
- **Supplier Dominance & Custom HBM:** Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix hold a global duopoly in combining DRAM and NAND stacking capabilities. HBM4 introduces "Custom HBM," shifting the industry from cyclical spot markets to long-term guaranteed supply agreements.
- **Chinese Competition:** *Dr. Kim Jung-ho* points out that CXMT is beginning HBM3 mass production, but a 3-to-5-year technological gap remains against Korean suppliers.
- **Korean Startups:** Local NPU players like Rebellion, FuriosaAI, and HyperAccelerator are receiving national fund backing to capture niche markets and reduce total reliance on Nvidia.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Future Memory Stack Integration:** By the era of HBM8 (around 2038), HBM and HBF will coexist as a multi-tiered memory complex serving GPUs. (*Dr. Kim Jung-ho*)
- **Ultimate 3D AI Computer Structure:** Future AI hardware will rely on a 3D stacked structure featuring HBM, HBF, and HBS under a cooled GPU on top, where power distribution networks and thermal cooling designs will dictate corporate survival. (*Dr. Kim Jung-ho*)
- **Financial Projections:** Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are on a realistic trajectory to hit a combined annual operating profit between 500 trillion and 600 trillion KRW amid the custom AI memory boom. (*Dr. Kim Jung-ho*)
- **Consumer Device Pricing:** Future AI smartphones and AIPC devices will see memory account for over half of their total hardware cost (e.g., 2 to 3 million KRW out of a 3 to 5 million KRW device). (*Dr. Kim Jung-ho*)

## Notable Quotes
> "AI equals memory. The capability of AI, the capability of an AI nation, and the data centers built for AI are ultimately determined by memory companies." 
> — *Dr. Kim Jung-ho*

> "Even if you deploy 1 million GPUs, they only work 10 to 20% of the time because they are waiting for data to arrive from the memory." 
> — *Dr. Kim Jung-ho*

> "In the future, HBM, HBF, and HBS will form a 100-story building with the GPU sitting right on top for cooling—that is bound to be the future structure of AI computers." 
> — *Dr. Kim Jung-ho*

briefings.title: IBM's $10 billion bet on what comes after AI (with CEO Arvind Krishna) | Masters of Scale
briefings.tldr: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna argues that the AI revolution is at "day zero," requiring enterprises to transition from experimenting with massive, expensive foundation models to deploying right-sized, economic alternatives.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna argues that the AI revolution is at "day zero," requiring enterprises to transition from experimenting with massive, expensive foundation models to deploying right-sized, economic alternatives. To lead the next wave of technological innovation, IBM is prioritizing hybrid cloud, cybersecurity, and a massive $10 billion commercial bet on quantum computing.

---

## Redefining AI Strategy: Moving Away from the "18-Wheeler"

*   **The Commodity of Foundation Models:** 
    *   **Low Switching Costs:** Krishna predicts that foundation models will become commodities within 1 to 3 years, meaning they will hold value (like gold or iron) but offer very little switching cost for enterprises.
*   **The "18-Wheeler" Analogy:** 
    *   **Over-Engineering Tasks:** Currently, enterprises are using massive, expensive AI models—the equivalent of an "18-wheeler"—for simple, everyday tasks like basic customer inquiries.
    *   **Shift to Right-Sized Models:** Within the next 24 months, rising token and GPU costs (which doubled in the six months prior to the interview) will force a transition to smaller, specialized, and on-premise models that operate at 1/100th of the cost.
*   **Strategic Lessons from Watson:** 
    *   **Monolithic Pitfalls:** Krishna candidly acknowledged IBM’s early missteps with Watson, noting that they built monolithic vertical solutions too quickly in the incredibly complex healthcare domain, despite having no sales experience dealing with doctors or the FDA.
*   **"Day Zero" Paradigm:** 
    *   **Focus at Scale:** Rather than running 100 small experiments, enterprises should select 3 to 5 high-impact use cases and execute them at scale to master change management and data organization.

---

## AI ROI, Productivity, and the Corporate Job Market

*   **The 20-80 Power Law:** 
    *   **Adoption Divide:** Unlike a 50-50 K-shaped economy, corporate AI adoption follows a power law where only 20% of companies aggressively adopt AI and achieve real returns, while 80% struggle to start.
    *   **Domain Experts over PhDs:** Companies do not need PhDs in computer science to deploy AI; instead, they should task curious domain experts with reimagining processes.
*   **IBM’s $5 Billion Efficiency Blueprint:** 
    *   **Delayed Return Curve:** During its first year of AI deployment, IBM spent more on engineers, infrastructure, and tokens than it saved. 
    *   **10x ROI:** By year two, IBM achieved a 10x return on its AI investments. The company is now on track to capture over $5 billion in productivity savings relative to its 2022 spending baseline.
*   **The Developer Productivity Paradox:** 
    *   **Increased Hiring:** IBM’s software developers became 40% more productive using AI, yet IBM tripled its college-level entry hiring. Lower development costs made previously unprofitable products economically viable, triggering net job growth.
    *   **Back-Office Displacement:** While value-generating sectors (sales, marketing, consulting, development) will grow, roughly 30% of back-office roles (compliance, accounts payable, procurement) will be displaced over the next few years.

---

## Cyber Defense and the Democratization of Threats

*   **Lowering the Attacker's Bar:** 
    *   **The Mythos Impact:** The release of advanced models like Anthropic's Mythos has dramatically lowered the technical barrier to entry for cyberattacks, expanding the global threat landscape to average-skilled bad actors.
*   **Project Lightwell:** 
    *   **$5 Billion Commitment:** To counter these threats, IBM launched Project Lightwell, a $5 billion initiative designed to identify and fix open-source vulnerabilities using AI.
    *   **Anonymized Clearinghouse:** IBM is deploying AI agents to automatically write security patches for open-source code and run an anonymized, collaborative defense utility for its clients.

---

## The $10 Billion Leap into Quantum Computing

*   **Government-Backed Scaling:** 
    *   **The Quantum Foundry:** IBM has partnered with the U.S. government on a new quantum foundry, investing $10 billion to scale commercial quantum systems.
*   **Exponential Performance Gains:** 
    *   **From Atoms to Proteins:** In a short timeframe, IBM’s quantum systems progressed from simulating a 5-atom molecule to a 300-atom molecule, and recently reached 12,000 atoms (simulating trypsin, a protein fragment). 
    *   **Disruptive Use Cases:** This rapid scaling will soon allow quantum computers to solve complex protein-binding equations in minutes, opening entirely new pathways for drug discovery, aerodynamics, and fluid dynamics.

---

## Overcoming Corporate Risk Aversion

*   **The Danger of No Risk:** 
    *   **Slow Corporate Decay:** Krishna warns that taking zero risk is a company's most dangerous path, leading to a slow, 5-to-10-year decline as competitors steadily erode the organization's most profitable business lines.
*   **Counteracting Loss Aversion:** 
    *   **Targeting 50% Probability Wins:** Because humans are naturally loss-averse, leadership must normalize failure. Krishna encourages teams to pitch projects with a 50% probability of success, rather than waiting for 90% certainty.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "An automobile is an automobile, at some gross level, if you step back. I guess you could take your kids to school in an 18-wheeler every morning. You could go milk shopping in an 18-wheeler. Then you'd ask yourself, is it really the most effective vehicle for that? ... Right now we're using the 18-wheeler for everything."  
> — *Arvind Krishna*

> "Actually, I recommend we give you somebody from a domain who doesn't really know the depth of AI, but who understands the difference AI could make to your domain. ... That's for the inventors of AI. That's not needed for the deployers of AI."  
> — *Arvind Krishna*

> "The most risky route is taking zero risk."  
> — *Arvind Krishna*

briefings.title: Investing Starts with Education | Material Matters with SEC Chairman Paul Atkins

people.name: John Moses
people.role: Director of the Office of Investor Education and Assistance

briefings.tldr: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman Paul Atkins and John Moses, Director of the Office of Investor Education and Assistance, discuss the critical importance of bottom-up financial education, highlighting the transformative rollout of tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts" for children and modern defense strategies against increasingly sophisticated AI and cryptocurrency scams.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman Paul Atkins and John Moses, Director of the Office of Investor Education and Assistance, discuss the critical importance of bottom-up financial education, highlighting the transformative rollout of tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts" for children and modern defense strategies against increasingly sophisticated AI and cryptocurrency scams.

---

## Fostering a Bottom-Up Investment Culture
* **Global Market Leadership:** The U.S. capital markets represent half of the world's total global capitalization. Chairman Atkins notes that international counterparts often ask how to replicate America's investing ethos, which he argues must be built from the bottom up rather than top down.
* **The "What We Own" Mindset:** 
    * Traditional personal finance focuses heavily on what people earn (income) and what they owe (debt). 
    * The SEC's educational mission focuses instead on what individuals *own*, positioning asset ownership as a core pillar of the American Dream as the nation approaches its "America 250" milestone.
* **Increased Personal Responsibility:** Market innovations have made investing more accessible than ever, coinciding with a shift where individuals are increasingly responsible for funding their own retirement, higher education, and long-term expenses.

## Grassroots Outreach and Financial Literacy Tools
* **Investor Assistance Services:** Through `help.sec.gov`, any American investor can submit inquiries to receive assistance in locating old 401(k) accounts, understanding financial products, or navigating problems with financial professionals (though the SEC does not provide specific investment advice).
* **Digital Tools on Investor.gov:**
    * **Compound Growth Calculator:** One of the most popular calculators on the web. Moses stresses that if financial assets are the "what" of investing, compound growth is the "why."
    * **DRIPs:** The SEC educates investors on the power of Dividend Reinvestment Programs to accelerate compound interest automatically.
* **Active Community Outreach:** 
    * The SEC conducts over 500 in-person and online outreach events annually, targeting military communities, older adults, high schools, colleges, and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs).
    * **Military Engagement:** Atkins and Moses recently visited Camp Pendleton in California, speaking to 200 new Marine recruits about saving, investing, and starting early to maximize their greatest asset: time.

## "Trump Accounts" and the Future of Youth Investing
* **The Core Concept:** A new legislative initiative designed to make every eligible child’s first financial account an investment account, shifting the cultural paradigm around early wealth generation.
* **Key Features and Benefits:**
    * **Seed Funding:** Eligible newborns receive $1,000 in government seed money. Moses advises families to "take the free money" by opening accounts promptly.
    * **Structural Guardrails:** Accounts are legally mandated to be low-fee, tax-advantaged, and diversified across broad-based index funds. 
    * **Long-Term Horizon:** Funds are locked until the beneficiary turns 18. Upon reaching adulthood, the accounts can naturally transition into traditional or Roth IRAs to build a foundation for retirement.
* **Philanthropic Integration:** The program allows private philanthropists to contribute to youth accounts. For example, the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation is actively contributing, and other donors are "adopting" entire states to fund local children's accounts.
* **Educational Impact:** A dedicated resource hub is available at `investor.gov/trumpaccounts` to help families integrate these accounts into their broader financial planning.

## Protecting Investors from Modern and AI-Driven Fraud
* **Digital Assets and Crypto Safety:** Digital assets represent the most common category of inquiry for the SEC's investor assistance team.
    * **Regulated Alternatives:** For investors seeking exposure to digital assets, the SEC highlights regulated options like exchange-traded products (ETPs) and ETFs rather than complex, unregulated instruments.
    * **Classic Red Flags:** Investors are urged to watch out for high guaranteed returns, high-pressure urgency, and pitches that sound "too good to be true."
* **Emerging Scam Trends:**
    * **AI and Impersonation Scams:** Scammers are using AI tools on an industrial scale to clone voices and mimic authority figures. The SEC recently issued an alert warning investors against bad actors using the likeness of SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce to endorse fraudulent products.
    * **Relationship and Romance Scams:** Often referred to as "long cons," these schemes build trust over time through business or personal relationships before introducing a fraudulent investment pitch.
    * **Affinity Fraud:** Scammers exploit trust within tight-knit communities, such as religious organizations, churches, and social clubs, to bypass investors' natural skepticism.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "If things like stocks and bonds and funds are the 'what' of investing, compound growth is really the 'why' of investing."  
> — *John Moses*

> "This idea of every child's first financial account being an investment account—it's really a big change in how we think about money... I think it has the prospect of really changing lives."  
> — *Paul Atkins*

> "We think actually the best defense against fraudulent crypto scams is good information and good awareness about investment basics overall, because many of the red flags of scams are similar or even the same."  
> — *John Moses*

briefings.title: Investing a $120 Billion Balance Sheet with No Outside Investors

people.name: Vlad Barbalat
people.role: President of Global Risk & Capital Solutions and CIO, Liberty Mutual Insurance

briefings.tldr: Vlad Barbalat, President of Global Risk & Capital Solutions and CIO at Liberty Mutual Insurance, manages a unique $120 billion balance sheet entirely free of third-party capital.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Vlad Barbalat, President of Global Risk & Capital Solutions and CIO at Liberty Mutual Insurance, manages a unique $120 billion balance sheet entirely free of third-party capital. This permanent-capital structure enables a highly resilient "fortress balance sheet" that prioritizes long-term investment hygiene, entrepreneurial risk-taking, and structural flexibility over short-term market pressures.

## The Power of a $120 Billion Permanent Capital Balance Sheet

* **Structural Autonomy:** Because Liberty Mutual is a mutual insurer, it operates without public shareholders demanding dividends or buybacks. This structural design allows the investment team to make long-term, value-driven decisions rather than expedient ones.
* **The Flywheel of Float:** Underwriting premiums are systematically funneled into the investment platform. By investing this capital to support the broader economy—such as funding infrastructure, real estate, and private credit—the firm strengthens its capital base, allowing it to underwrite larger, more complex, and long-tailed risks.
* **Capital Allocation Breakdown:** The $120 billion balance sheet is segmented into two primary components:
    * **Reserves (~$70–$75 Billion):** Tightly managed to ensure policyholder promises are met. Rather than passively holding low-yield bonds, LMI actively optimizes this portfolio to act as a dynamic liquidity provider in the markets.
    * **Surplus Capital (~$45–$50 Billion):** Allocated across "growth credit" (leveraged corporate credit, direct lending, asset-backed finance) and "growth equity" (private equity, real estate, energy, and infrastructure).

## Investment Philosophy: "Prepare, Not Predict"

* **Agnostic to Macro Forecasting:** LMI deliberately avoids tactical macro forecasting. Instead, the firm focuses on building a resilient, long-term portfolio capable of weathering diverse economic eventualities.
* **A Multidimensional Toolkit:** Unlike traditional LPs constrained by rigid product mandates, LMI evaluates the exposures it desires first, then determines the best acquisition channel—whether via direct lending, co-investments, club deals, or backing specialized GPs.
* **The "Branded Capital" Proposition:** LMI positions itself as an agile, creative, and highly responsive partner for general partners (GPs). 
    * **Relationship Velocity:** The team operates with the speed of a GP rather than a slow-moving corporate LP, establishing LMI as a primary hub for off-market, highly structured transactions.
    * **Strategic Philanthropy:** LMI frequently acts as a connector, facilitating valuable, non-monetary introductions between business partners without requiring direct financial involvement.

## From Soviet Moldova to American Agency

* **The Immigrant Perspective:** Having immigrated to the US from Soviet-era Moldova in 1990 at age nine, Barbalat attributes his investment worldview to the profound contrast between oppressive systems and American individualism. 
    * **Persecution to Agency:** Surviving anti-Semitic persecution in the USSR shaped a mindset characterized by zero entitlement and a deep appreciation for the permissionless innovation of the US.
* **The Croissant Analogy:** Barbalat highlights America's unique economic engine through the lens of human creativity: while the Soviet system viewed bread as a mere utility, the US market allows individuals to endlessly iterate, perfect, and commercialize something as simple as a croissant.
* **Fostering Institutional Entrepreneurship:** To prevent the complacency typical of large insurance firms, Barbalat has intentionally structured LMI's culture to incentivize curiosity and calculated risk-taking, ensuring the team remains hungry to "make things better."

## Navigating the Invisible Future: AI, Volatility, and Private Markets

* **The Valuation Paradox:** Rapid technological disruptions (especially AI) and shifting geopolitical supply chains make the long-term future highly unpredictable. This uncertainty is driving internal debates about whether corporate valuation multiples should be structurally lower across all industries.
* **Creative Destruction by 2030:** LMI anticipates massive corporate turnarounds by the end of the decade, predicting that multiple trillion-dollar companies of 2030 do not yet exist, while several current hundred-billion-dollar giants will completely disappear.
* **Credit Duration Risk:** While short-term corporate debt (under four years) remains highly secure, holding 30-year paper on legacy tech giants (such as Oracle or Salesforce) carries significantly higher structural risk due to the threat of AI disintermediation.
* **The Public-Private Divide:** LMI maintains a strong preference for private equity over public markets. Private markets now offer the scale and prestige of public markets without forcing executive teams to sacrifice long-term strategy for quarterly earnings compliance.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "We're not in the business of predicting the future, we're in the business of being prepared for all its eventualities." — Vlad Barbalat

> "The level of agency you have as a citizen of the US or as a resident of the US is unparalleled to anywhere else in the world... If you have talents, if you have motivation, there's an infinite amount of ways you can both define what success is, define how you will contribute, and ultimately live a life where you have the option to thrive." — Vlad Barbalat

> "You will likely have trillion-dollar companies in 2030 that currently don't exist. And you probably have trillion-dollar companies or many hundred-billion-dollar companies that will not exist." — Vlad Barbalat

> "My leadership team knows that transparency is what allows you to have autonomy. No transparency, no autonomy." — Vlad Barbalat

briefings.title: Mark Pincus: How to Spot a Fake CEO
briefings.tldr: Zynga founder Mark Pincus outlines the frameworks required to build enduring consumer products, emphasizing the importance of separating winning instincts from mediocre execution, utilizing "founder mode" to maintain intellectual honesty, and training "technical assistants" to scale a founder's decision-making style.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Zynga founder Mark Pincus outlines the frameworks required to build enduring consumer products, emphasizing the importance of separating winning instincts from mediocre execution, utilizing "founder mode" to maintain intellectual honesty, and training "technical assistants" to scale a founder's decision-making style.

---

## Separating Instincts from Ideas: The "Proven, Better, New" Framework

*   **Instincts vs. Ideas:** Founders must separate winning human instincts (identifying emotional pain points or broken experiences) from specific product ideas, which are often mediocre. 
    *   **The B+ Trap:** A B+ idea is the enemy of an A instinct. Sticking heroically to a B+ idea distracts founders from finding the true "A" execution.
    *   **Historical Misses:** Pincus registered *smstaxi.com* in the early internet era, proving his instinct was right (foreshadowing Uber), but his execution idea was wrong. Similarly, his early social network, *tribe.net*, failed despite correct social media instincts.
*   **The "Proven, Better, New" Framework:**
    *   **Proven:** Deconstruct what has already worked for the exact target audience in the market.
    *   **Better:** Introduce highly visible, incremental improvements (e.g., free/half price, no download friction) that 10 out of 10 users immediately appreciate.
    *   **New:** Introduce a high-risk, novel element to capture attention. Isolating the "new" prevents the product from failing for the wrong reasons.

## Mastering User Retention in a Brutal App Economy

*   **The Modern Landscape:** The current consumer app market is incredibly difficult. Users download an average of zero new apps per month. Out of 40,000 games launched in the App Store last year, 0% sustained a top 25 position.
*   **Day 365 Retention:** Success requires building products that users can picture themselves using a year from now. 
*   **The Zynga Playbook:** Rather than trying to force new user behaviors, builders should meet users where they already hang out (e.g., MySpace and Facebook in 2007; X and ChatGPT today).
    *   **Social Loops & Status:** Zynga utilized social mechanics to drive daily retention. The ultimate high-value reward was social connection—Zynga even tracked real-world marriages that resulted from players meeting in *Words with Friends* or *FarmVille*.

## "Founder Mode" vs. The Trap of the "Fake CEO"

*   **The CEO’s Real Job:** A CEO's core responsibility is to work directly with product teams to build experiences users love. Pincus tracked his own calendar with advisor Bing Gordon to ensure at least 50% of his time was dedicated to core product work.
*   **Identifying "Fake CEOs":** "Fake" CEOs prioritize the global speaking circuit, public relations, and lecturing about culture over product development. 
    *   **On Culture:** Pincus believes corporate culture is like *Fight Club*—if you are actively trying to manufacture or talk about it scientifically, you are likely failing to live it.
*   **Founder Mode:** True founder mode is having the courage and intellectual honesty to make highly unpopular decisions against investors and your own team.
    *   *Examples:* Jeff Bezos launching Amazon Prime despite heavy pushback from his CFO, or Elon Musk completely restarting xAI after realizing early iterations were built incorrectly. 

## Technical Assistants: Scaling the Founder's "Vampire Blood"

*   **The Technical Assistant (TA) Role:** Originating with Andy Grove and Bill Gates, and popularized by Jeff Bezos, the TA role is a high-potential product track rather than an administrative Chief of Staff role.
*   **Passing the "Vampire Blood":** TAs shadow the CEO in every meeting to absorb their unique decision-making framework and "vampire blood." They are eventually deployed to run major product spin-offs as mini-CEOs (e.g., Andy Jassy starting AWS/Alexa under Bezos).
*   **The Ian Cinnamon Case Study:** Pincus recruited Cinnamon from MIT. When the Zynga poker team wanted to let Cinnamon go because he was "too entrepreneurial" and ignored bad directions, Pincus pulled him out to be his TA. Cinnamon went on to incubate his own companies and currently runs Apex.

## AI Maximalism and Market Realities

*   **No Obvious Consumer Distribution:** While Pincus is an AI maximalist, he notes that consumer AI is currently tough to invest in due to lack of organic distribution, with only a few outliers like Midjourney and Suno finding sustainable footholds.
*   **The Enterprise Advantage:** Pincus co-founded **Hivemind** alongside Reid Hoffman and Ratankar Das. The enterprise startup focuses on the "first and last mile" of AI integration, recognizing that human interaction is still required to handle edge cases and system-of-record updates.
*   **Trillion-Dollar Scale:** Unlike the 2000 dot-com bubble, which was built on non-viable companies like *pets.com*, today's AI GPUs are running hot with massive, real utility and rapid ARR generation. Pincus predicts $2T to $5T megacaps will scale to $10T to $20T.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Your number one job as a founder is to be right." 
— Mark Pincus

> "B+ is the enemy of an A. B+ often, if we stick with it, is taking up space, it's distracting us from unlocking the A, and to fail or to call the ball that that idea isn't that good, in itself is really powerful." 
— Mark Pincus

> "I like to say hopefully your mission doesn't ever change and your vision maybe rarely changes and your strategy changes as often as it needs to and your tactics probably change every day in order to win." 
— Mark Pincus

> "I think culture is one of those things that's like Fight Club, like you don't talk about it... Trying to manufacture a culture to me is a fake CEO thing." 
— Mark Pincus

briefings.title: Nature Is Infrastructure

people.name: Razan Al Mubarak
people.role: President, International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
people.organization: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)

organizations: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
briefings.tldr: Integrating natural capital into economic strategy is a core driver of long-term business competitiveness, profitability, and talent attraction.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Integrating natural capital into economic strategy is a core driver of long-term business competitiveness, profitability, and talent attraction. To secure future prosperity, leaders must transition from regulatory compromises like "net zero" to absolute decarbonization ("real zero") while deploying advanced biological and technological innovations.

## Redefining Ecological Conservation and Capital
*   **Pragmatic Adaptation over Restoration:** Angela Moles (Professor of Ecology and Chair of the New South Wales Threatened Species Scientific Committee) argues that conservation must move away from trying to restore ecosystems to a historical, pre-colonization ideal. Because climate change makes past baselines obsolete, policies must focus on maximizing the biodiversity and biomes we can actively carry forward.
*   **Systemic Financial Reporting:** André Hoffmann (Vice-Chairman of Roche Holding and Co-Chair of the World Economic Forum) emphasizes that businesses are flying blind by only measuring financial flows. To prevent depleting foundational resources, companies must adopt standardized reporting systems—such as an integrated profit and loss account—that account for impacts on natural, human, and social capital.
*   **Aligning Corporate Purpose:** Hoffmann asserts that for industries like pharmaceuticals, saving human lives is fundamentally linked to preserving natural systems, which supply essential molecules, clean water, and clean energy. 

## Decoupling Growth from Fossil Fuels
*   **The Economic Power of Biology:** Ester Baiget (President and CEO of Novonesis) highlights that the biological transition is already commercially viable. In the 1980s, generating $100 of GDP required one barrel of oil; today, it takes less than half. Novonesis leverages biological solutions (enzymes, microbes, and proteins) to replace fossil fuels, chemicals, and fertilizers with biodegradable alternatives.
*   **Proving Planet-Profit Alignment:** Novonesis has reduced its carbon emissions by 63% since 2018 while growing revenue by more than 30% and maintaining a 37% EBITDA margin, demonstrating that planetary stewardship and corporate profitability are mutually reinforcing.
*   **Securing Top-Tier Talent:** Baiget notes that committing to planetary health is a primary driver for attracting younger generations of workers, who prioritize employment at companies that actively align with their values.
*   **The Case for "Real Zero":** Andrew Forrest (Executive Chairman and Founder of Fortescue) strongly critiques "net zero" frameworks and carbon credits, calling them bureaucratic loopholes that enable continued fossil fuel burning. He demands a commitment to "real zero"—the complete cessation of fossil fuel combustion.

## Industrial and Engineering Innovations
*   **Heavy Industry Electrification:** Fortescue is systematically greening its heavy operations, transitioning massive haul trucks and 3-kilometer-long, 30,000-ton transport trains to green energy. This shift eliminates the use of 1 billion liters of diesel annually, directly boosting the company's bottom line.
*   **Sparing Ground Resources:** Danny Cheng Jing (Global VP of Jinko Solar) details how solar innovation has increased cell efficiency from 15% to 27% over the past decade. This technology increases energy density, reducing the physical land footprint required for solar installations by 60% to 70%.
*   **Off-Grid and Space Infrastructure:** To bypass terrestrial land constraints, Jinko Solar is investing in Building Integrated PV (BIPV) and researching space-based solar infrastructure, such as solar-powered satellites and orbital data centers. 
*   **Smarter Resource Consumption:** Forrest argues that massive infrastructure projects, like data centers, should not plug into public grids and water mains. Instead, they should operate off-grid on cheap, open land, utilizing green energy to run reverse-osmosis systems that generate more water and power than the facility consumes.

## Overcoming Policy Failures and Geopolitical Obstacles
*   **Eradicating Perverse Subsidies:** Panelists criticized the estimated $3 trillion in annual global fossil fuel subsidies, which artificially distort the market and force clean technologies to compete with one hand tied behind their back. 
*   **National Security as a Transition Driver:** Decarbonization is increasingly propelled by national security and energy independence rather than climate policy alone. Countries like India, Brazil, Indonesia, and China are aggressively scaling localized, homegrown green energy to decouple from volatile fossil fuel import routes.
*   **Scaling Green Hydrogen and Ammonia:** Forrest urges nations—specifically China—to support the International Maritime Organization (IMO) proposals to mandate green fuels. Achieving green hydrogen production at $2 per kilogram would immediately make green ammonia highly competitive against fossil fuels for shipping and agriculture.

## Notable Quotes

> "If you do [economic growth] at the expense of nature, it's a short-term win at best."  
> — *Angela Moles*

> "If we continue to destroy the planet, we are going to go with it."  
> — *André Hoffmann*

> "We are showing the world that planet, profitability, and growth are two sides of the same coin."  
> — *Ester Baiget*

> "We are going green because it's good business, baby."  
> — *Andrew Forrest*

briefings.title: Renminbi and the World
briefings.tldr: The internationalization of the Renminbi (RMB) has shifted from a prestige project to a critical strategic resilience effort, achieving substantial progress in cross-border trade settlements but remaining constrained as a global store of value by China's capital controls.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The internationalization of the Renminbi (RMB) has shifted from a prestige project to a critical strategic resilience effort, achieving substantial progress in cross-border trade settlements but remaining constrained as a global store of value by China's capital controls.

***

## The Strategic Evolution of RMB Internationalization
*   **Shift from Prestige to Resilience:** **Zoe Liu** highlights that RMB internationalization has transitioned from a status symbol to a vital strategic project designed to build economic resilience and insulate China from geopolitical risks.
*   **A Twenty-Year Cumulative Effort:** **Zhu Ning** stresses that recent milestones are the result of a two-decade-long process, supported by a decade of building offshore clearing centers and standardizing financial products, rather than a short-term policy push.
*   **The Global South’s Focus on Diversification:** For middle powers like South Africa, transacting in RMB is driven by a desire to avoid systemic vulnerabilities rather than picking sides in a bipolar currency regime.
    *   **Bilateral Swaps:** The South African Reserve Bank and the People's Bank of China (PBOC) have maintained a bilateral currency swap agreement since 2015 to buffer short-term balance-of-payment pressures.
    *   **Direct Clearing Infrastructure:** In November 2023, South Africa’s Standard Bank became the first African bank authorized to clear and settle transactions directly in RMB through the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS).

## Measuring RMB Performance: The Three Functions of Money
*   **Means of Exchange (High Progress):** The RMB has made significant inroads as a payment currency, particularly in bilateral trade with major partners.
    *   **Sino-Russian Trade:** Approximately 99% of bilateral trade between China and Russia is now settled in local currencies, primarily the RMB.
    *   **Cross-Border Settlement:** Between 60% and 80% of China’s own cross-border trade is now settled in RMB.
    *   **The "Invisible" SWIFT Shift:** **Diana Choyleva** notes that while SWIFT data suggests RMB usage has slightly dipped in global payments, this is misleading. An increasing volume of RMB trade has moved entirely off traditional Western "dollar rails" to CIPS and digital currency platforms like mBridge, escaping SWIFT visibility.
*   **Unit of Account (Emerging Potential):** China is actively promoting RMB-denominated commodity contracts—including copper, Shanghai oil futures, Guangzhou lithium, and Ganzhou rare earths—to establish the currency as a benchmark in non-oil energy markets.
*   **Store of Value (Limited Progress):** Despite trade gains, the RMB accounts for less than 2% of official global foreign exchange reserves (compared to the U.S. dollar's 58%), primarily due to China's strict capital controls.

## Currency Stability, Valuation, and Exchange Rate Regimes
*   **Managed Flexibility vs. Market Forces:** The PBOC is gradually engineering a "two-way fluctuation" exchange rate mechanism. **Zhu Ning** explains that "stability" in this context refers to a predictable, market-reflective mechanism rather than a fixed exchange rate.
*   **Predictability and Geopolitical Backing:** **Zoe Liu** argues that the PBOC has successfully maintained currency predictability since the end of COVID-19. Despite domestic economic weaknesses, the RMB has avoided competitive devaluation because of its role as a strategic resilience tool.
*   **The Manufacturing-Currency Disconnect:** A stark gap exists between China's industrial footprint and its currency status. China commands nearly 30% of global manufacturing power but holds under 2% of global currency reserves. 

## Addressing the Shortage of Safe Assets and Investment Channels
*   **Expanding Bond Markets:** While China lacks a risk-free benchmark equivalent to U.S. Treasuries, it has rapidly expanded its municipal and corporate bond markets over the last 20 years to offer viable fixed-income alternatives.
*   **The Green Transition Advantage:** **Zoe Liu** suggests that as the global energy mix diversifies away from oil, China’s primary financial benchmark advantage will lie in green bonds and transition finance, heavily backed by its massive domestic industrial capacity.
*   **Bypassing Controls via "Connect" Schemes:** To attract foreign capital without fully opening its capital account, China is leveraging regulated investment pathways like the Bond Connect and Stock Connect programs, linking mainland exchanges with Hong Kong and London.

## The Evolving Roles of Hong Kong and Shanghai as Financial Hubs
*   **Complementary Financial Roles:** Rather than competing destructively, Shanghai and Hong Kong have established distinct operational zones:
    *   **Shanghai:** Focuses on onshore wealth management, supporting the domestic economy, and managing onshore exchange rates.
    *   **Hong Kong:** Functions as the world’s largest international wealth management center, facilitating two-way global investment flows.
*   **Internationalizing Capital Controls:** **Diana Choyleva** argues that Beijing's crackdowns on illicit cross-border retail brokerages actually strengthen Hong Kong's position. The crackdowns signal that while illegal capital flight is blocked, legitimate capital will increasingly flow through Hong Kong via regulated connect schemes, essentially allowing China to internationalize its capital controls on its own terms.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "The biggest change for RMB internationalization is that it has transformed from more of a prestige project to a very important strategic and resilience project."  
> — **Zoe Liu**, Senior Fellow, Council on Foreign Relations

> "The critical thing is not to create single points of dependency but rather to focus on diversification. And for us, the future obviously is diversified and not necessarily bipolar between two hegemons and currencies."  
> — **Ashor Nick Sarupen**, Deputy Minister of Finance, South Africa

> "We are not in a position where there are significant bilateral exchange rate moves that have no connection to what the dollar is doing. We're still very much in that dollar-tethered global system, and one that will change at the margin depending on which country ends up in which sphere of geopolitical influence."  
> — **Diana Choyleva**, Founder and Chief Economist, Enodo Economics
